metadata.name: rect
metadata.description: (x, y, w, h [, fill] [, stroke] [, lineWidth]) - a canvas rectangle op. pass to canvas(): =canvas(200, 80, rect(0, 0, 200, 80, "#1a1a2e")).

metadata.name: text
metadata.description: (x, y, text [, fill] [, font]) - a canvas text op (baseline at x,y). =text(12, 24, "hi", "#fff", "16px system-ui").

metadata.name: line
metadata.description: (x1, y1, x2, y2 [, stroke] [, lineWidth]) - a canvas line segment op.

metadata.name: circle
metadata.description: (x, y, r [, fill] [, stroke] [, lineWidth]) - a canvas circle op.

metadata.name: wedge
metadata.description: (cx, cy, r, a0, a1 [, fill] [, stroke] [, lineWidth]) - a canvas pie-slice op from angle a0 to a1 (radians, clockwise from 3 o'clock). The piechart fn stacks these.

metadata.name: frames
metadata.description: (points, r?, period?, fill?, box?) - an ANIMATED canvas op: a dot of radius r steps through the trajectory points ([[x,y],…]) once per period seconds; box strokes a frame border. The painter's rAF loop drives it. The simulate verb computes a def-driven trajectory and emits through this.

metadata.name: canvas
metadata.description: (width, height, ...ops) - a <canvas> drawn from rect/text/line/circle/wedge ops; the painter replays them onto the 2d context. use as a cell value or inside mount/dom. op LISTS flatten in, so chart fns compose: =canvas(420, 260, barchart(t!A2:A8, t!B2:B8)).

metadata.name: dragdrop
metadata.description: (w?, h?) - two drop zones (A, B) + a rectangle you drag between them; it snaps to the nearest zone on release. A value vnode; the interactivity lives in the canvas renderer (the draggable/zone ops).
